act_name: Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001

definitions.meaning: The act of engaging, directly or indirectly, in a transaction that involves proceeds of an unlawful activity.
Any person, including branches and subsidiaries, listed in the First Schedule required to comply with reporting obligations.
The process of identifying and verifying the customer's identity and assessing the risks associated with the business relationship.

obligations.name: Suspicious Transaction Reporting
obligations.description: Reporting institutions must promptly report any transaction that gives reason to suspect it involves proceeds of an unlawful activity.

obligations.name: Customer Due Diligence (CDD)
obligations.description: Institutions must conduct CDD when establishing business relations or when a transaction exceeds the prescribed limit.

obligations.name: Record Keeping
obligations.description: Maintain all records of transactions and CDD information for at least 6 years.

procedures.name: Submission of Suspicious Transaction Report (STR)
steps: Submit STR to BNM via FINS system
procedures.conditions: Must be submitted within 24 hours of confirmation of suspicion.

offences.description: Engaging in, abetting, or conspiring to commit money laundering.
Disclosing to any person that a report has been made or that an investigation is being carried out.

penalties.corporate_penalty: Fine up to RM 5 million or 5 times the value of proceeds, whichever is higher

recordkeeping_requirements.conditions: From the date the transaction is completed or business relationship is terminated.

exemptions: Low-risk products as defined in guidelines

exceptions.description: Simplified CDD allowed for public listed companies and government entities.

cross_references.description: Detailed guidelines on implementing AMLA requirements.
Global standards which AMLA 2001 aims to comply with.
